articles.title: शिवम् सिमेन्टमा अनुबन्धित नेपाली स्प्रिन्टर आयुष कुँवरद्वारा ३० वर्ष पुरानो राष्ट्रिय कीर्तिमान भंग
articles.summary:
शिवम् सिमेन्टमा अनुबन्धित नेपाली स्प्रिन्टर आयुष कुँवरले २०० मिटर दौडमा ३० वर्ष पुरानो राष्ट्रिय कीर्तिमान तोड्दै नयाँ इतिहास रचेका छन्। अमेरिकाको लस एन्जलसमा आयोजित वर्ल्ड एथलेटिक्स स्वीकृत प्रतियोगितामा उनले २१.८७ सेकेन्डमा २०० मिटर दूरी पूरा गर्दै सन् १९९५ देखिको record भङ्ग गरेका हुन्। त्यसपछि अगस्ट ९, २०२६ मा लण्डनमा सम्पन्न अर्को प्रतियोगितामा आफ्नै रेकर्ड सुधार्दै उनले २१.६६ सेकेन्डको नयाँ कीर्तिमान कायम गरे। यसअघि उनले ६० मिटर दौडमा पनि ७.०२ सेकेन्डको राष्ट्रिय रेकर्ड बनाइसकेका छन्।

सन् २०२५ मा दक्षिण कोरियामा भएको एसियाली एथलेटिक्स प्रतियोगिताका क्रममा ह्यामस्ट्रिङ चोटका कारण प्रतिस्पर्धाबाट बाहिरिनुपरे पनि आयुषले कठिन पुनरागमन गरेका हुन्। सीमित स्रोतसाधन, चोटपटक र संस्थागत चुनौतीहरूका बाबजुद निरन्तरको मेहनत र अनुशासनका कारण उनले एक वर्षपछि यो ऐतिहासिक सफलता हासिल गर्न सफल भए।

नेपाली खेलकुद क्षेत्रमा अवसर र पूर्वाधारको अभाव कायमै रहँदा पनि आयुषले स्वयं पहल गरेर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका प्रतियोगिताहरूमा सहभागिता जनाउँदै आएका छन्। हाल अमेरिकामा प्रशिक्षणरत उनले आफ्नो खेल जीवन र दैनिक व्यवस्थापन आफैँ गर्दै नेपाली एथलेटिक्सलाई नयाँ उचाइमा पुर्‍याउने प्रयास गरिरहेका छन्।

यस सफलतामा शिवम् सिमेन्टको महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको छ। सन् २०२३ देखि आयुषको खेल यात्रामा सहयात्रा गर्दै आएको शिवम् सिमेन्टले उनलाई हवाई टिकट, पोशाकलगायत आवश्यक आर्थिक तथा भौतिक सहयोग उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको छ।

कीर्तिमान कायम गरेपछि आयुषले ३० वर्षसम्म रेकर्ड कायम रहनु नेपाली खेलाडीले अवसर नपाउनुको परिणाम भएको बताएका छन्। नयाँ खेलाडीहरूलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न उनले 'स्प्रिन्ट प्रोजेक्ट' नामक निजी योजना ल्याउने तयारी गरिरहेका छन् भने शिवम् सिमेन्टले पनि आगामी दिनमा नेपाली खेलकुद र अन्य प्रतिभावान खेलाडीहरूलाई सहयोग निरन्तर राख्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको छ।

articles.title: किमदेखि एलिनसम्म : विदेशीको भिसा, विवाह र गतिविधिको डरलाग्दो रिपोर्ट
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । विदेशी नागरिक नेपाल घुम्न, व्यापार गर्न वा अध्ययनका लागि आउने गरेका छन् । तर अध्यागमन र सुरक्षा निकायको अनुसन्धानले यसरी आउने केही विवाह, भाषा केन्द्र र एनजीओको आवरणमा धार्मिक प्रचारदेखि शंकास्पद गतिविधिसम्म गरेको देखाएको छ । पिटर क्वाङ सियोङ किमदेखि एलिन बिट ब्रोगस्ट्रोमसम्मका घटनाले राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामाथि गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएको छ ।

विदेशी नागरिक नेपाल किन आउँछन् ? यसको सामान्य जवाफ हा घुम्न, व्यापार गर्न, अध्ययन गर्न, व्यवसाय गर्न वा नेपालमा केही समय बस्न । तर अध्यागमन विभाग र सुरक्षा निकायको अनुसन्धानले केही विदेशीको नेपाल बसाइँको उद्देश्य सामान्यभन्दा निकै फरक र गम्भीर हुनसक्ने देखाएको छ । यसको एउटा उद्धाहरण हुन्, दक्षिण कोरियाली मूलका अमेरिकी नागरिक पिटर क्वाङ सियोङ किम । उनी विगत एक महिनादेखि अध्यागमन विभागको हिरासतमा थिए । तर सर्वोच्च अदालतले बन्दीप्रत्यक्षीकरण रिटमाथि फैसला गर्दै उनलाई थुनामुक्त गर्न आदेश दिएको छ ।

किम सन् २०१३ देखि नेपाल आउजाउ गर्दै आएका थिए । नेपाली महिला निलम बर्देवासँग विवाह गरेपछि उनले वैवाहिक भिसासमेत लिएका थिए । तर अध्यागमन विभागले उनलाई साउनमा एक वर्ष नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न नपाउने गरी देश निकाला गरेको थियो ।

त्यसविरुद्ध उनकी श्रीमतीले सर्वोच्चमा रिट दायर गरेकी थिइन् । किममाथिको अनुसन्धानमा भने उनको गतिविधि धार्मिक प्रचार, भिसाको दुरुपयोग र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षासँग जोडिएको विषयमा केन्द्रित देखिन्छ । अनुसन्धान अनुसार किमले दोलखाको चरिकोटमा भाषा केन्द्र सञ्चालन गरेका थिए ।

सन् २०१८ मा भीमेश्वर बहिरा आधारभूत विद्यालयमा क्रिश्चियन धर्म प्रचार गरेको र तत्कालीन प्रधानाध्यापकलाई धर्म परिवर्तन गराएको आरोपसमेत अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ । काभ्रेको नमोबुद्धमा रहेको द लाइट एन्ड सल्ट स्कुलमार्फत् विपन्न बालबालिकालाई लक्षित गरेर धर्म प्रचार गरिएको दाबी पनि गरिएको छ ।

त्यस्तै दोलखा, सिन्धुली र काभ्रेमा धार्मिक गतिविधि विस्तार गर्ने, स्थानीय अवस्था र भविष्यमा लगानी गर्नुपर्ने क्षेत्रबारे रिपोर्ट तयार पारेर विदेशस्थित संस्थामा पठाउने गरेको अनुसन्धानमा भेटिएको बताइएको छ । यसका लागि उनले अमेरिकामा रहेका संस्थाहरुबाट आर्थिक सहयोग पाउने गरेका थिए ।

मिसनरी कार्यलाई निरन्तरता दिनकै लागि रणनीतिक रूपमा उनले व्यावसायिक भिसालाई विवाह भिसामा परिणत गर्ने योजना बनाएको देखिन्छ । उनको वैवाहिक सम्बन्ध नेपालमा दीर्घकालीन बसोवास गर्ने र आफ्नो कानुनी हैसियत जोगाउन मात्र प्रयोग भएको देखिन्छ ।

अनुसन्धानमा सन् २०२२ को नेपाल मिसन रिपोर्ट पनि फेला परेको बताइएको छ । बिजनेस भिसामा बस्दा उनले गरेको गतिविधि थाहा पाएर डिपोर्ट हुनसक्ने जोखिमका कारण वैवाहिक भिसा लिने योजना बनाइएको २०२२ नेपाल मिसन रिपोर्टमा उल्लेख भएको अध्यागमनको दाबी छ । किम ७२ वर्षका र उनकी नेपाली श्रीमती ३० वर्षकी रहेको तथा किमको अमेरिकामा समेत परिवार र सन्तान रहेको अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ ।

किमजस्तै अरु को को ?

तर यस्तो विषय किममा मात्रै सीमित छैन । स्वीडेनी नागरिक एलिन बिट ब्रोगस्ट्रोमको विषय पनि अनुसन्धानमा आएको छ । ५१ वर्षीया एलिनले २४ वर्षीय वीरगञ्ज घर भएका अनिकेतकुमार डंगोलसँग २०७९ भदौ ६ गते काठमाडौँ जिल्ल्ला अदालतबाट विवाह गरी त्यसैको आधारमा जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय पर्साबाट नेपाली अंगीकृत नागरिकता लिएको र त्यसपछि सम्बन्धविच्छेद गरेको अनुसन्धानमा देखिएको छ ।

अनुसन्धान अनुसार दुवैबीच खासै चिनजान थिएन र विवाहपछि पनि श्रीमान श्रीमतीको रूपमा बसेको पनि देखिएन । आर्थिक प्रलोभनमा कागजी विवाह भएको आशंका गरिएको छ ।

एलिनले पछि अर्का विदेशी नागरिकसँग विवाह गरिन् र उनलाई समेत नेपाल ल्याएको अनुसन्धानमा भेटिएको छ । उनले स्वीडेनी नागरिकता त्यागेको दाबी गरेपनि त्यसको प्रमाण पेस नगरेको बताइन्छ । नेपाली राहदानी प्रयोग गरेर भारत १६ पटक गएको र त्यहाँबाट स्वीडिस राहदानीमार्फत तेस्रो मुलुक गएको विवरणसमेत अनुसन्धानमा आएको छ ।

एलिनका विदेशी श्रीमानले गोफिका इन्टरनेसनल कार्गो प्रालि नामको कम्पनी २०८० जेठ १४ गते उद्योग विभागमा दर्ता कम्पनी खोलेर बिजनेस भिसा लिएको तर कारोबार नगरी कम्पनी बन्द गरेको विवरण पनि अनुसन्धानमा छ । नेपाली नागरिकता लिएकी एलिनले नेपाली युवासँग सम्बन्ध बिच्छेद गरी पुन आफ्नै श्रीमानसँग विवाह गरेको पाइएको छ । यसै विवाहको आधारमा उनले श्रीमान कार्ललाई समेत नेपाली अंगिकृत नागरिकता समेत दिलाउन सफल भएको पाइन्छ । एलिनसँग नेपालमा विहे गर्नु अघि कार्ल ११ पटक पर्यटक र ५ पटक व्यवसायिक भिसामा नेपाल आइसकेका थिए ।

एलिनका श्रीमानले नेपाली अंगीकृत नागरिकता लिँदासम्मको सबै विवरणहरू शंकास्पद रहेको देखिन्छ । यसबारे राष्ट्रिय अनुसन्धान विभागले अनुसन्धान गरेर रिपोर्ट पनि दिएको छ । तर कानुनी रूपमा उनीहरूले सबै प्रक्रिया पूरा गरेर नेपाली नागरिकता समेत लिएकाले कारबाही प्रक्रिया भने अघि बढाउन सकेको छैनन ।

अर्को उदाहरण अमेरिकी नागरिक अमान्ड मैडा समर्स हुन् । उनले ९२ वर्षीय हर्कबहादुर घर्तीसँग विवाह गरेर वैवाहिक भिसामा नेपाल बसेकी थिइन् । उनी १५ वर्षजति नेपालमा बसेकी थिइन् ।

विवाहपछि अमान्ड ललितपुर महानगरपालिका–२५, सैंबुमा बसिन् र सन्ध्या कर्णको नाममा दर्ता भएको स्वालम्बन नामक एनजीओमा आबद्ध भइन् । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा उनले पाकिस्तानी नागरिक लर्ड किङ भिन्सेन्टलाई नेपालमा सेल्टर दिएको खुलेको बताइएको छ । भिन्सेन्ट २०२५ जनवरी २८ मा नेपाल आएका थिए र उनको पर्यटक भिसा मे १२ सम्म मात्रै थियो । तर भिसा सकिएको करिब एक महिनासम्म अमान्डले उनलाई आश्रय दिएको अनुसन्धानमा भेटियो ।

गुप्तचर सूचनाका आधारमा २०८३ जेठ २९ गते सैंबुबाट उनीहरू पक्राउ परे र पछि डिपोर्ट गरिए । अध्यागमन विभागका अनुसार सन् २०२५ मा मात्रै ५२३ विदेशी नागरिक डिपोर्ट भएका छन् ।

तीमध्ये चीनका १२०, बंगलादेशका ७५, अमेरिकाका ३५, बेलायतका २२, पाकिस्तानका १८ र अन्य देशका २५३ नागरिक छन् । ४५९ जना ओभरस्टे र ६४ जना शंकास्पद गतिविधिका कारण डिपोर्ट गरिएको विभागको तथ्यांक छ ।

यसरी डिपोर्ट गरिएकाहरु मध्यै धेरैले पहिला अध्ययन भिसा, व्यवसायिक भिसाको बहानामा लामो समय नेपालमा बसेर मिसनरीको रूपमा काम गर्ने प्रवृत्ति देखिएको छ । काठमाडौंलाई नेस्ट अफ स्पाई भनिन्छ । विभिन्न देशका गुप्तचर एजेन्सीहरूको ट्रान्जिट र सूचना संकलन केन्द्रका रूपमा समेत काठमाडौंलाई प्रयोग गर्ने गरिएको सुरक्षा विश्लेषण छ ।

नेपालमा हुने गतिविधिमा चिनियाँ चासो वा अमेरिकी रणनीतिक उद्देश्यका लागि सूचना संकलनका काम गरेको हुनसक्ने सुरक्षा संयन्त्रको विश्लेषण छ । त्यसैले पर्यटन, व्यवसाय, भाषा केन्द्र, एनजीओ वा विवाहको आवरणमा लामो समय बस्ने र त्यस क्रममा धार्मिक प्रचार, शंकास्पद गतिविधि वा राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामा असर पार्ने काम हुन सक्ने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: ‘गोदावरी महिला उद्यम विकास प्रतिष्ठान’को उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गोदावरी नगरपालिकामा नवनिर्मित ‘गोदावरी महिला उद्यम विकास प्रतिष्ठान’को आइतबार एक विशेष समारोहबीच उद्घाटन गरिएको छ ।

महिलाहरूलाई सीप विकास, उद्यमशीलता र आयआर्जनका अवसरहरूसँग जोड्दै आर्थिक रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बनाउने उद्देश्यले प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना गरिएको हो । गोदावरी नगरपालिकाका उपप्रमुख मुना अधिकारीको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त कार्यक्रममा नगर प्रमुख गजेन्द्र महर्जन प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी थिए ।

कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वडाका वडाध्यक्ष, जनप्रतिनिधि, महिला उद्यमी, सरोकारवाला संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि तथा स्थानीयको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो । समारोहमा स्थानीय महिला उद्यमीहरूले उत्पादन गरेका विभिन्न सामग्रीको प्रदर्शनीसमेत गरिएको थियो ।

नवनिर्मित प्रतिष्ठानलाई महिला उद्यमीहरूका लागि तालिम, उत्पादन, प्रदर्शनी तथा बजारीकरणको एकीकृत केन्द्रका रूपमा विकास गर्ने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

गोदावरी नगरपालिकाले महिलाहरूलाई शिक्षा, सीप र उद्यमशीलतामार्फत आत्मनिर्भर बनाउन अनौपचारिक शिक्षा कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन कार्यविधि २०८१ समेत जारी गरी अभियान सञ्चालन गरिरहेको छ । हालसम्म ४७ जना महिलाले प्लस टु उत्तीर्ण गरिसकेका छन् भने ११ जना स्नातक तहमा अध्ययनरत छन् ।

यस्तै, १४० भन्दा बढी महिला तह १ र २ मा अध्ययन गरिरहेका छन् । शिक्षाका साथै महिलाहरूलाई आयआर्जनमा जोड्न नगरपालिकाले ढाका बुनाई, साबुन तथा सरसफाइ सामग्री निर्माण, सिलाइ–कटाइ, हस्तकला, अचार, टपरी र स्यानिटरी प्याड उत्पादनजस्ता विभिन्न सीपमूलक तालिमहरू सञ्चालन गर्दै आएको छ ।

महिलाहरूलाई केवल तालिममा मात्र सीमित नराखी शिक्षित, सीपयुक्त, स्वरोजगार र पूर्ण रूपमा आत्मनिर्भर बनाउनु यस अभियानको लक्ष्य रहेको छ ।

articles.title: दोलखामा दिनभर धार्मिक परिक्रमा, रातभर लाखे नाच !
articles.summary:
दोलखा । प्राचीन तथा ऐतिहासिक नगरी दोलखामा धार्मिक सहिष्णुता र सांस्कृतिक सद्भावको प्रतीक मानिने परम्परागत हिले जात्रा अर्थात् गुउँला पर्व हर्षोल्लासका साथ मनाइँदैछ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदा अर्थात् घण्टाकर्ण (गाठामा) को तेस्रो दिनदेखि सुरु भएको यो ऐतिहासिक पर्वका कारण यतिबेला दोलखा बजार २४ सै घण्टा सांस्कृतिक रौनकमा झुमिरहेको छ ।

बिहानैदेखि गुञ्जने परम्परागत बाजा, धार्मिक परिक्रमा र दिउँसोदेखि रातिसम्म देखाइने फरक स्वरूपका लाखे नाचले प्राचीन नगरी दोलखा यतिबेला गुञ्जायमान बनेको छ । घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् स्थानीय भाषामा ‘गाठामा’को तेस्रो दिन, श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि दोलखामा गुउँला जात्राको औपचारिक सुरुवात हुन्छ ।

माथिल्लो र तल्लो टोलका बेग्लाबेग्लै डापा खलक परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित बिहानै सांस्कृतिक परिक्रमामा निस्कन्छन् । स्थानीय भाषामा देउ उय भनिने यो परिक्रमा कागे अष्टमीका दिन समापन हुन्छ ।

पूजा सामग्री बोकेका ज्येष्ठ नागरिकसहितको टोली स्वयंभू चैत्य र कोर्छे टोलबाट सुरु भई भीमेश्वर, कालीमन्दिर, त्रिपुरा सुन्दरी, राजकुलेश्वर तलेजु, नक्छे चैत्य, गणेश मन्दिर र मच्चिछन्द्रनाथ मन्दिर हुँदै पुनः स्वयंभू चैत्य पुगेर टुंगिन्छ । जात्रा मनाउँदा हिन्दू र बौद्ध दुवै धार्मिकस्थलको समान रूपमा परिक्रमा गरिन्छ ।

दिउँसोदेखि दोलखा बजारमा लाखे नाचको रौनक सुरु हुन्छ । एउटै जात्रामा चार फरक स्वरूपका लाखे प्रदर्शन हुने भएकाले दोलखाको लाखे देशभरमै विशेष मानिन्छ ।

दिउँसो ३ देखि ५ बजेसम्म ‘जोङ डाकस’ निकालिन्छ । यसमा हात दुई जना दाउरेले समातेर दर्शकलाई लखेट्दै मनोरञ्जन गराउँछन् । आसुरी शक्तिमाथि विजयको कथा भन्ने नेपाल डाकस भने राति मात्र नाचिन्छ । वर्षमा एक दिन रक्षाबन्धनका दिन निकालिने ‘ड्वाकु डाकस’ ठूलो लाखे हो । फरक मुखुण्डो लगाइने यसलाई महाकालीका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ ।

गाईजात्रादेखि पञ्चमीसम्म ‘माझीपा डाकस’ पनि प्रदर्शन गरिन्छ । डोरीले बाँधेर लाखेलाई नचाउने र माझीहरूले नियन्त्रण गर्न खोजेको लोककथाको अभिनय यसमा देखाइन्छ । पुस्तौँदेखि चल्दै आएको यस अमूर्त कला र संस्कृति संरक्षणमा स्थानीय युवाको सक्रियता उदाहरणीय छ ।

articles.title: माननीयको अभिब्यक्तिले सुरक्षा संगठनको बदनाम
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मुलुकको शान्ति, सुरक्षा र कानुन कार्यान्वयनको मुख्य जिम्मेवारी बोकेको नेपाल प्रहरी अहिले दोहोरो दबाबमा परेको छ । एकातिर गत बर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गतेको आन्दोलनका क्रममा संगठनले भोगेको भौतिक तथा मनोवैज्ञानिक क्षतिको असर अझै पूर्णरूपमा मेटिन सकेको छैन भने, अर्कोतिर राजनीतिक वृत्तबाटै संगठनको नेतृत्व र कार्यशैलीमाथि प्रश्न उठाउने क्रम तीव्र बनेको छ ।

राज्यकै प्रमुख निकायहरु कार्यपालिका र ब्यवस्थापिकाबाटै प्रहरी संगठनको बदनाम गर्ने कार्यले संगठनको मनोबल झनै गिराएको छ । सार्वजनिक पदमा बसेका व्यक्तिले उठाउने प्रश्नले सधैं सार्वजनिक चासो निम्त्याउँछ, विशेषगरी त्यो प्रश्न राज्यको कुनै संवेदनशील निकायविरुद्ध उठाइएको हुँदा गत बुधबार सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको बैठकमा रास्वपाका सांसद खगेन्द्र सुनारले नेपाल प्रहरीको सामग्री खरिद प्रक्रियामा प्रश्न उठाउँदै प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई नै कठघरामा उभ्याए ।

जुत्ता, मोजा, पोशाकदेखि लाठी खरिदसम्ममा आर्थिक अनियमितता भएको आशय दिँदै उनले तत्काल निष्पक्ष छानबिनको माग गरे । आइजीपी कार्कीले तत्काल प्रतिवाद गरे । खरिद प्रक्रियामा कुनै अनियमितता नभएको दाबी गर्दै तथ्यहीन आरोप लगाएर कर्मचारीको मनोबल कमजोर नबनाउन आग्रह गरे ।

त्यसपछि सांसद सुनारकै आफ्नै कानुनी पृष्ठभूमिबारे सार्वजनिक बहस सुरु भयो — प्रश्न उठाउने व्यक्ति स्वयं कति चोखो छ ? आईजीपी कार्कीले सांसद सुनारविरुद्ध नै आएका उजुरीहरूको चाङ औंल्याए । सुनारविरुद्ध माननीयदेखि दयनीयसम्मका व्यक्तिहरूले विभिन्न प्रकृतिका उजुरी दिएको र, आरोपको पोको खोलिदिन सक्ने चेतावनी दिए ।

सर्वत्र आलोचित खगेन्द्र अझै ‘अराजक’

लेखा समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीमाथि खगेन्द्र सुनारले उठाएको प्रश्नले मात्रै खगेन्द्र चर्चा र विवादमा आएका होइनन् । प्रहरी संगठन विरुद्ध पटक पटक सार्वजनिक उनको अभिब्यक्तिले सांसद सुनार आलोचित छन् ।

२०८३ वैशाख ७ गते सिन्धुली सुनकोशी गाउँपालिका–३ जुम्लीडाँडा निवासी २३ वर्षीय श्रीकृष्ण विक खुर्कोटस्थित प्रहरीको हिरासतमै मृत्यु भएको घटनामा जनप्रतिनिधिको हैसियतमा सिन्धुली पुगेका सुनाले एकतर्फी आरोप लगाउँदै सिन्धुलीका एसपीको कठालो नै समातेर घिसार्नुपर्ने अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए ।

सांसद हुनुपूर्व सुनारले एक वर्षअघि माइतीघरबाट समेत जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसर काठमाडौंका एकजना डीएसपी विरुद्ध अर्मयादित अभिव्यक्ति दिएका थिए । त्यो बेला जहाँ पनि उनी हातमा नेल र निधारमा नवसेना लेखिएको फेटा बाँधेर सांकेतिक विरोधमा देखिन्थे । यो पटक संसदीय समितिमा आईजीपी कार्कीविरुद्ध पनि उही शैलीमा आक्रोश पोखेका थिए ।

सुनारविरुद्ध तीन मुद्दा अदालतमा विचाराधिन

सांसद खगेन्द्र माथि अहिले पनि तीनवटा मुद्दा अदालतमै विचाराधीन छ । दैलेखको नारायण नगरपालिका–२ भैसेखोरका खगेन्द्र प्रतिनिधि सभाको चुनावमा भने बाँके क्षेत्र नम्बर ३ बाट निर्वाचित भएका हुन् । उनीमाथि सुर्खेत प्रहरीले २०८० को असारमा पक्राउ गरेर सार्वजनिक शान्तिविरुद्धको कसुरमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

त्यो बेला जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय सुर्खेतले २० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी लिएर छाडेको थियो । त्यसको एक वर्षपछि पुनः २०८१ असारमै सुर्खेतकै अस्पतालका डाक्टरहरुमाथि अभद्र व्यवहार तथा तोडफोडको मुद्दा हाल सुर्खेत जिल्ला अदालतमा विचाराधीन अवस्थामा छ । २०८२ साउनमा काभ्रेकी एक महिलामाथि सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत चरित्र हत्या गर्ने खालको पोष्ट गरेको आरोपमा उनीमाथि काभ्रे प्रहरीले साइबर अपराधमा मुद्दा चलाएको थियो ।

साउन ५ गते पक्राउ पुर्जी लिए पनि उनी पक्राउ भने परेनन् । पछि मुद्दा अदालत दर्ता भएपछि उनी काभ्रे जिल्ला अदालतमा हाजिर भएका थिए । काभ्रे अदालतले समेत सुनारलाई ५० हजार रुपैयाँ धरौटी बुझाएर मात्रै छाड्ने आदेश गरेका थिए । हालसम्म पनि मुद्दा टुंगो लागेको छैन ।

सुनारको प्रहरी नेतृत्वमाथि भएको व्यक्तिगत आक्षेप र अमर्यादित व्यवहार विवाद गृहमन्त्री हुँदै सभामुखसम्म पुगेको छ । आइजिपीसहित आठ एआइजी र एक डिआइजीले प्रहरी संगठनकै मनोबल खस्किएको भन्दै संसदीय छानबिनमा विधि र मर्यादा पालना गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन् ।

बेनामे उजुरीको भरमा संसदीय समितिमा बोलाएर संगठनकै मानमर्दन हुने गरी हुर्मत लिएको गुनासो समेत गरेका छन् । प्रहरी अधिकारी मात्र होइन, गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङसमेत सुनारको ब्यवहारले रुष्ट छन् ।

प्रहरी संगठनबाटै ‘माननीय’विरुद्ध खेद ब्यक्त

प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्य सुनारको अराजक अभिब्यक्तिको सिंगो प्रहरी संगठनले नै खेद प्रकट गरेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरी पूर्वप्रहरी संगठन प्रमुख मञ्चले विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर सुरक्षा निकाय र यसको नेतृत्वमाथि भएका व्यक्तिलक्षित टीकाटिप्पणीप्रति खेद प्रकट गरेको छ ।

भने पूर्वप्रहरी कर्मचारी परिषद्, पूर्वसशस्त्र प्रहरी संघ र सुरक्षा तथा न्याय अध्ययन केन्द्रले संयुक्त विज्ञप्ति जारी गरेर यस्ता गतिविधिले सुरक्षाकर्मीको मनोबल खस्कने र राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षामै असर पर्ने स्पष्ट गरेका छन् । साथै ती संस्थाहरूले संसदीय समितिमा बोलाउँदा पदीय गरिमा, सम्मान र व्यावसायिक मर्यादा कायम राख्न सुझाएका छन् ।

अझै पुरिएको छैन भदौ २४ को घाउ

नेपाल प्रहरीका लागि २०८२ भदौ २३ र २४ गते घटनाको घाउ अझै पुरिएको छैन । त्यो घटनाले संगठनको भौतिक संरचना, हतियार, कार्यालय र प्रहरी कर्मचारीको सुरक्षामाथि नै ठूलो चुनौती खडा गरेको छ ।

उक्त आन्दोलनका क्रममा काठमाडौँ उपत्यकाका मात्र १ सय ५३ प्रहरी कार्यालयमा आगजनी, १७ वटा प्रहरी वृत्त क्षतिग्रस्त,१ हजार १ सय हतियार लुटिपाट,३ जना प्रहरीको मृत्यु र प्रहरी कर्मचारीले ज्यान जोगाउन बर्दी फुकालेर भाग्नुपर्ने अवस्था आएको थियो ।

सुरक्षा संगठन र कर्मचारीको मनोबल बढाउनुपर्नेमा सत्तारुढ दलबाट नै यस्ता खाले अभिव्यक्तिले संगठनको मनोबल गिर्दो अवस्थामा पुगेको पूर्व प्रहरी अधिकारीको भनाई छ ।

सांसदको काम प्रश्न उठाउनु नै हो, तर प्रश्न उठाउने नाममा प्रमाणविनाका आरोप लगाउनु र आरोप प्रमाणित नहुँदै त्यसलाई सत्यका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्नु जिम्मेवार राजनीतिक अभ्यास होइन । खगेन्द्र सुनार हिजो आन्दोलनकारी भए पनि आज जनताका प्रतिनिधि हुन् ।

त्यसैले विना आधार राज्यको जिम्मावार निकायहरुको बदनाम गर्दा सुरक्षा संगठनको मात्र होइन, स्वयम् माननीयको ओज घटाउँछ । प्रहरीलाई प्रश्न गरौँ, तर प्रमाणसहित ।

प्रहरीलाई जवाफदेही बनाऔँ, तर संस्थागत रूपमा । प्रहरी कमजोर हुँदा कमजोर हुने प्रहरी प्रमुख मात्र होइन, सिंगो राज्य हो । प्रहरी संगठनका भित्रका कमजोरीहरु सुधार हुनु पर्छ नै, सांसद सुनारको आफू पनि सुध्रिन जरुरी छ ।

articles.title: पूर्वी नाकाबाट विदेशी पर्यटक बढे, सबैभन्दा धेरै भुटानी
articles.summary:
झापा । पूर्वी नेपालको प्रमुख स्थलमार्ग काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा ८६ देशका ९ हजार ४४७ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल भित्रिएका छन्। अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाको तथ्याङ्कअनुसार यो संख्या दैनिक औसत करिब २६ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेको हो ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा काँकरभिट्टा नाकाबाट नेपाल प्रवेश गर्ने विदेशी पर्यटकमा भुटान, अमेरिका, थाइल्याण्ड, अष्ट्रेलिया, बेलायत, क्यानडा, जर्मनी, फ्रान्स, जापान र रुसलगायत देशका नागरिक छन् । कुल आगन्तुकमध्ये भुटानी नागरिकको हिस्सा सबैभन्दा ठूलो छ । ४ हजार ९९४ जना भुटानी नागरिक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् ।

जुन कुल पर्यटक संख्याको करिब ५३ प्रतिशत हो । त्यस्तै २ हजार १५२ जना अमेरिकी नागरिकले काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । यो कुल आगन्तुकको करिब २३ प्रतिशत हो । भारतका नागरिकलाई नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न भिसा आवश्यक नपर्ने भएकाले उनीहरूलाई तेस्रो मुलुकका पर्यटकसम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्कमा समावेश गरिएको छैन ।

महिनागत तथ्याङ्कअनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी विदेशी पर्यटक पुसमा १ हजार ८५० जना र सबैभन्दा कम भदौमा २१६ जना नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । अध्यागमन कार्यालयले पुस र माघलाई प्रमुख पर्यटकीय याम मानेको छ ।

पर्यटकको आगमन उत्साहजनक भएपनि बसाइ छोटो हुने गरेको होटल व्यवसायी बताउँछन। पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यमा पर्यटकलाई केही दिन रोक्न सके झापा, इलाम, ताप्लेजुङलगायत जिल्लाको पर्यटन तथा होटल व्यवसायमा उल्लेख्य योगदान पुग्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ छ ।

पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार र सीमा नाकामै यातायात, होटल तथा भ्रमणसम्बन्धी सूचना उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने पर्यटन व्यवसायी कुन्दन निरौला बताउँछन् ।

अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाले सन् २०२४ अगस्टदेखि पूर्ण रूपमा अध्यागमन सेवा सञ्चालन गरेको थियो । सेवा प्रभावकारी भएपछि विदेशी पर्यटकको आगमन क्रमशः बढेको सूचना अधिकारी इन्द्रकुमार राजवंशी बताउँछन् ।

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार, पर्यटन सूचना केन्द्र र आकर्षक प्याकेज निर्माणसँगै संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहबीच समन्वय गर्न सके विदेशी पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउन सकिने देखिन्छ । यसबाट होटल, यातायात, ट्राभल्स, हस्तकला तथा स्थानीय उत्पादनको बजारसमेत लाभान्वित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: राँगाको सिङबाट बन्ने गुँला पर्वको मुख्य बाजा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेवार समुदायका विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीको प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक पर्व गुँला बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । एक महिनासम्म मनाइने पर्वमा भक्तजनले परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित चैत्य, विहार र मन्दिरको परिक्रमा गर्दै बुद्धको पूजा–आराधना गर्ने गर्दछन् ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका परम्परागत नेवार वस्ती र टोलहरुमा अब एक महिनासम्म सडक वा गल्लीहरुमा विहान मानिसहरुको चहलपहल शुरु नहुँदै सुनिने छ, धिमे, भुस्या, बाँसुरी र न्याकुँको सुमधुर आवाज । अनि बाजाको यही धुन पछ्याउँदै मानिसहरू चैत्यतर्फ अघि बढिरहेका हुने छन् । यो गुँला पर्वको अवसरमा देखिने दृश्य हो ।

नेवार समुदायमा पनि विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीले मनाउने गुँला पर्व बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि भाद्र शुक्ल प्रतिपदासम्म चल्ने यो पर्व करिब एक महिनासम्म धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।

गुँला शब्दको अर्थ आफैमा रोचक पनि छ । नेपाल भाषामा ‘गुँ’ को अर्थ नौ र ‘ला’ को अर्थ महिना भन्ने गरिन्छ । नेपाल संवतको नवौँ महिनामा मनाइने भएकाले यसको नाम गुँला रहन गएको मानिन्छ । गुँलाको वास्तविक आकर्षण बिहानै सुरु हुने यात्रामा देखिन्छ । भक्तजनहरू परम्परागत बाजा बजाउँदै विभिन्न चैत्य, विहार, बहाः र बहीको परिक्रमा गर्छन् ।

काठमाडौंको स्वयम्भू, बौद्ध, पाटनलगायतका धार्मिक तथा ऐतिहासिक स्थलमा गुँला पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखिन्छ । एउटा समूह धिमे बजाउँदै अघि बढिरहेको हुन्छ । यसमा कसैले भुस्या बजाइरहेको हुन्छ भने कसैले न्याकुँको गहिरो आवाज निकालिरहेको हुन्छ । यही दृश्यले गुँलालाई काठमाडौँका अन्य धेरै जात्रा र पर्वहरुभन्दा फरक बनाएको छ ।

गुँला पूजा र परिक्रमा गर्ने पर्व मात्रै होइन । संगीत जोडिएको उपत्यकाको जीवित संस्कृति पनि हो । विशेषगरी न्याकुँ बाजा गुँलाको पहिचानसँग जोडिएको छ । राँगाको सिङबाट बनाइने यो बाजा हेर्दा साधारण देखिए पनि यसको ध्वनि निकै विशिष्ट हुन्छ ।

परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक यात्राहरुमा यसको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ । त्यसैगरी धिमे, बाँसुरी, भुस्या र धाः लगायतका बाजासँगै बज्दा यी आवाजले पनि गुँला पर्वमा सांगीतिक समूहको स्वरूप लिन्छन् । पछिल्लो समय यस्ता जात्रा पर्वमा नयाँ पुस्ताको सहभागिता पनि बढिरहेको छ । नयाँ पूस्ताको सहभागितासँगै परम्परागत पर्व र संस्कृति पुस्तान्तरण पनि हुँदैछन् ।

गुँला धार्मिक पर्व मात्रैमा सीमित छैन । सामाजिकरुपमा खेतीपातीको मुख्य काम सकिएको समयसँग पनि यो पर्व जोडिएको छ । मानिसहरू केही फुर्सदिला हुने यही समयमा समुदाय भेला हुने, भेटघाट गर्ने र सामूहिक रूपमा धार्मिक गतिविधिमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पनि गुँलाले जुटाइ दिएको छ ।

बौद्ध परम्परामा वर्षायामको साधना र धार्मिक अभ्याससँग पनि गुँला समयको सम्बन्ध जोडिन्छ । त्यसैले यो अवधि पूजा, ध्यान, पाठ, दान र पुण्यकर्मका लागि विशेष मानिन्छ । यसको अर्को पक्ष के भने गुँला पर्वमा हुने चैत्य परिक्रमा एउटा यात्रा मात्रै होइन ।

उपत्यकाका विभिन्न स्थानीय धार्मिक स्थललाई जोड्ने सांस्कृतिक नेटवर्क जस्तो पनि हो । एउटा टोलबाट अर्को टोल, एउटा बहाःबाट अर्को चैत्यसम्म बाजाको धुनले यी ठाउँहरूलाई जोडिरहेको हुन्छ । काठमाडौंलाई मन्दिरै–मन्दिरको सहर भनिन्छ । तर गुँला पर्वले कामठाडौँ बाजा, बहाः, बही र चैत्यहरूको पनि सहर हो भन्ने प्रमाण पनि दिन्छ । एक महिनासम्म बज्ने यी बाजाहरु पुर्खाको स्मृति हुन्, धार्मिक आस्था हुन् र पहिचानको आवाज हुन् ।

articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: Election Commission begins study on out-of-country, inter-district voting
articles.summary:
The Election Commission has revived efforts to allow Nepali citizens living abroad and outside their registered constituencies to vote, eight years after the Supreme Court ordered the government to make necessary arrangements.

The commission is examining the legal, technological and administrative arrangements required to introduce what is broadly known as external voting.

Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who met election officials at the commission headquarters on Friday, assured them that the government would support the necessary legislation, infrastructure and technology for the reform.

“Start the preparations and tell us clearly what the government needs to do,” an election official quoted Gurung as telling the commissioners. “Whether it requires legal amendments or technological infrastructure, give us a clear action plan. The government is ready to provide the necessary support.”

The move comes as political parties, youth activists and civil society groups have renewed demands for voting arrangements for Nepalis who live, work or study away from their permanent constituencies, particularly those living overseas.

The issue gained momentum following last year’s Gen Z movement. Ahead of the general elections on March 5 this year, activists and civil society groups campaigned for external voting, arguing that millions of Nepalis living outside the country should not be excluded from elections.

The commission was unable to introduce such arrangements for the March elections, citing a lack of time, the absence of enabling legislation and insufficiently tested electronic voting infrastructure.

The commission’s new leadership has now made electoral inclusion a priority. Chief Election Commissioner Man Bahadur Karki, appointed along with two other commissioners last month, had included voting rights for overseas Nepalis and internal migrants in his work plan presented during his parliamentary hearing.

Speaking at the commission on Friday, Karki said two high-level committees had been formed to determine how the voting system could be implemented.

“This issue has been raised for a long time, and public demand has increased in recent years. Furthermore, the apex court has issued explicit directions on the matter,” Karki said.

“Maximising voter participation is fundamental to a vibrant democracy. The study panels will determine how we can practically manage voting for citizens living overseas or away from their registered home addresses.”

The commission formed the two committees at its board meeting on August 12. The first, led by commissioner Guru Prasad Wagle, will examine the legal framework. It will review existing election laws and propose amendments needed for voter registration abroad, polling stations in foreign countries, the appointment of overseas polling officials and legal recognition of ballots cast outside Nepal.

The second committee, headed by commissioner Rajiv Subba, will examine technology and operational arrangements. Its work will include assessing information technology infrastructure, digital security, administrative logistics and possible voting methods, including physical ballots, postal voting and secure electronic voting.

The committees will draw expertise from several government agencies. The legal panel will include representatives from the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The technology panel will include technical officials from the foreign ministry, the Integrated Data Management Centre and the Cyber Bureau of Nepal Police.

Commission spokesperson Narayan Prasad Bhattarai said the coordinators of the two committees had already begun preliminary work. The committees are expected to hold their first full meetings next week after the concerned ministries nominate their representatives.

The commission’s latest initiative follows a Supreme Court directive issued on March 23, 2018 for the government and the Election Commission to make the necessary legal and technical arrangements to enable eligible Nepali citizens living abroad to exercise their voting right.

More than eight years later, Parliament has yet to enact the primary legislation needed to implement the directive. Existing election laws do not provide for voter registration outside Nepal, polling stations abroad, voting through diplomatic missions or electronic balloting.

Implementing external voting would be a major logistical undertaking. Nepali citizens live in around 170 countries, requiring the government and election authorities to establish mechanisms that can operate across different jurisdictions and comply with local laws.

Wagle said his committee would study international practices, treaty obligations and previous feasibility reports before recommending a legal framework.

The commission has previously examined external voting in 2010-11 and 2016-17. Both studies found that the system was logistically challenging but technically possible if introduced in phases and backed by coordination among government agencies.

The 2010-11 study estimated that nearly 4 million Nepalis were living abroad at the time. The number has increased substantially since then. A separate study by the Policy Research Institute before the March 5 elections also concluded that out-of-country voting was feasible if appropriate legal and regulatory arrangements were put in place.

The commission does not envisage introducing external voting simultaneously in every country where Nepalis live. Instead, the study committees will identify countries with large Nepali populations and functioning diplomatic missions as possible locations for an initial pilot.

Gurung has also urged the commission to pursue a phased approach and identify jurisdictions where external voting could be introduced first.

The commission is considering the November 2027 provincial assembly elections as a possible opportunity to test external voting under the proportional representation system, provided Parliament passes the required legislation in time.

Local elections are scheduled for April-May 2027, followed by provincial assembly elections in November 2027. The commission therefore faces a tight timetable if it wants to introduce even a limited external voting system during the next election cycle.

For the reform to become operational, however, legal changes will be essential. The commission can develop technical and administrative models, but Parliament must first create a legal basis for registering voters abroad, establishing polling arrangements outside Nepal and recognising votes cast from outside a voter’s registered constituency.

articles.title: Nepal, India to use modern technology for border surveillance
articles.summary:
Nepal and India have agreed to use modern technology, including closed-circuit television (CCTV) and other equipment, to strengthen security surveillance in sensitive areas along the border.

The understanding was reached at the 14th meeting of the Nepal-India Joint Working Group (JWG) on Border Management, which concluded on Friday in Dehradun, India. The Nepali delegation was led by Home Ministry Joint Secretary Ananda Kafle, while the Indian side was led by Paushumi Basu, joint secretary at India’s Ministry of Home Affairs.

“Both sides agreed to enhance security surveillance in sensitive border areas through the use of modern and latest technology, including CCTV and other modern equipment,” the Nepali Embassy in New Delhi said in a statement.

The two sides will hold further discussions on the use of such technology, including its deployment and operation by security agencies on the ground, according to a Nepali official who participated in the meeting.

The meeting focused primarily on border security, cross-border crime, trade and other issues of mutual concern. The two sides agreed to strengthen coordination and real-time information-sharing among relevant agencies to combat cross-border crimes, including the trafficking of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, prohibited and controlled medicines, wildlife, and people.

They also discussed economic crimes, including the circulation of counterfeit currency, arms and ammunition smuggling and other illegal activities. The Nepali side raised emerging security challenges such as cybercrime and cross-border digital fraud.

The two sides also discussed measures to strengthen security arrangements and infrastructure along the Nepal-India border and improve coordination and information-sharing among security agencies. Issues of radicalisation and religious fundamentalism, disaster risk reduction and management, and border infrastructure were also discussed.

According to Nepali officials, the meeting also featured talks on removing encroachments from no-man’s-land, unauthorised trade, and Indian assistance to Nepali security agencies. Capacity building of Nepal’s security institutions was also on the agenda.

Nepal also renewed its request for India to recognise its national identity card as a valid travel document for travel between the two countries.

India is positive about the proposal but has sought more time to consider it, according to a Nepali official.

The two sides also reviewed decisions taken by lower-level security mechanisms involving chief district officers on the Nepali side and district magistrates on the Indian side, as well as the Armed Police Force and India’s Sashastra Seema Bal.

Issues related to radicalisation, religious fundamentalism, activities of third-country nationals and tightening border security have routinely featured in security meetings between Nepal and India, from home secretary-level talks to meetings between chief district officers and district magistrates.

The two countries also have a permanent local-level mechanism, the Border District Coordination Committee, to address security concerns in border districts.

articles.title: A single shot can prevent JE, but Nepal’s vaccination programme leaves adults out
articles.summary:
Sayal Rai was just 12 years old when he contracted Japanese encephalitis. Now 14, he remains in a permanent vegetative state and has been on ventilator support ever since, first at Birat Medical College and Teaching Hospital in Biratnagar and later at BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences, Dharan.

“It's already been more than two years since the infection, and my son is still on a ventilator,” Nirmala, Sayal’s mother, a resident of Belaka Municipality in Udayapur district, told the Post over the phone from Dharan. “He cannot breathe on his own or speak, and has developed wounds on his back from lying in the same position.”

Japanese encephalitis (JE) is a viral brain infection that kills about one-third of those who develop severe illness, while up to half of survivors are left with severe, lifelong disabilities, according to the World Health Organisation.

Nepal is currently in the midst of a major JE outbreak that has killed at least 21 people and infected 59 others in the past six weeks.

Sayal is among scores of survivors whose lives have been permanently altered by the disease.

Nepal’s routine JE vaccination programme covers children but leaves adults out, even though they account for most infections and deaths. Officials are now considering expanding the vaccine to adults, but say funding remains a big obstacle.

“He sheds tears when secretions lodge in his throat and trigger coughing, or when he experiences severe pain,” said Nirmala. “It is deeply distressing to watch him suffer. He is our only child, and we had pinned all our hopes for our bright future on him.”

Sayal was in the sixth grade when he contracted the virus. His parents had enrolled him in a private school at the district headquarters and arranged for him to stay in a rented room with his cousin sister.

When he developed a 104-degree fever, they rushed him to Birat Teaching Hospital in Biratnagar. Doctors admitted him to the intensive care unit after his condition deteriorated.

His parents spent around Rs800,000 on his treatment, but he showed no signs of recovery. They eventually transferred him to BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences after they could no longer afford the mounting bills.

“We owe around Rs4 million to the hospital, and the hospital administration has since moved him to a free bed because we could no longer afford his treatment.”

As Sayal’s stay in the hospital stretched from weeks into months and then years, much of his care fell to his family. He depends on continuous oxygen support and has a tube inserted through his neck for feeding. He also needs assistance with excretion and almost every other basic bodily function.

Nirmala, once a housewife who also worked on her family’s farm in the village, has become his full-time caregiver. She has learned to perform many tasks normally carried out by nurses, including monitoring his condition, managing his feeding tube, tending to his wounds and caring for him round the clock.

She has rented a small room near the hospital for Rs2,000 a month where she prepares gruel from rice or flour, along with milk and eggs, and feeds him through the tube. Initially, relatives visited and provided some financial assistance, but their visits and support gradually dwindled.

Nirmala has borrowed money from relatives but does not know how she will repay the loans. Her husband, who once shared the burden of caring for their son, now carries sand near the India border to make ends meet. He is often unreachable because of a poor phone network.

“We can’t say anything about Sayal’s full recovery,” said Dr Basanta Rai, assistant professor and consultant paediatrician at the BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences. “But his mother has not given up hope and has invested everything she has in her son.”

Dr Rai said Sayal’s mother has been paying for medicines, diapers, wound ointments, and other items that are not covered by the hospital’s free services.

“JE is not like other diseases. Those who suffer know the real consequences,” said Dr Rai. “It can leave survivors with devastating, lifelong disabilities and have a huge impact on their families.”

JE is transmitted to humans through the bite of infected Culex mosquitoes.

Since the JE outbreak began, 21 people have died, and 59 others have been infected. Nepal’s current case fatality rate is around 25 percent. Eighty percent of JE infection cases have been reported from 59 local units in 25 districts. Of those infected, 89 percent were unvaccinated. Among those who died, 81 percent were above 50, and were all unvaccinated, government data show.

According to the Ministry of Health and Food Safety, Koshi province has recorded 24 cases, including 10 deaths. Madhesh has reported 19 cases and six deaths, Lumbini seven cases and two deaths, Sudurpaschim 13 cases and two deaths, and Bagmati reported 10 cases and one death. Gandaki saw five cases, while Karnali recorded one case.

Jhapa district in Koshi province recorded 10 cases, six of which were fatal. Its case fatality rate of 60 percent is the highest in the country. Parsa, Nawalparasi and Ilam districts have each recorded a case fatality rate of 50 percent. Parsa has reported four cases, including two deaths. Nawalparasi and Ilam each reported two cases, including two deaths.

Kailali has reported seven cases and two deaths; Morang seven cases and one death; Saptari six cases and two deaths; Sunsari five cases and two deaths; Dang three cases and one death; and Dhanusha three cases and one death.

Last year, 41 people died, and 141 others were infected with JE, which had spread to over 117 local units in 45 districts. The case fatality rate was around 23 percent. In 2024, 23 people, including one person in Kathmandu Valley, died of JE, while at least 80 were infected.

Health officials say most of those infected or killed by JE were unvaccinated. Many were adults not covered by Nepal’s routine childhood immunisation programme. Such people are at serious risk of severe illness and death. JE can cause permanent damage to the brain and nervous system, and there is no specific treatment. Care focuses on managing symptoms and complications.

Last year’s data show that 76 percent of those who died from JE were over 40, while around 70 percent of those infected were older than 15. The figures indicate that the disease also affects many people outside the age group covered by routine childhood vaccination.

JE has long been a major public health problem in Nepal. The virus killed nearly 2,000 people in Nepal in 2005, mostly children in the Tarai districts.

Nepal started administering the JE vaccine in 2006, eight years before the WHO officially issued prequalification certification, due to high rates of infection and deaths. The programme was later expanded with support from donors and global health partners.

Nepal now includes the JE vaccine in its routine immunisation programme and provides it free of cost to children at state-run health facilities. But the programme does not cover adults, even though it has been killing many adults in recent years.

“We can prevent death and disability from JE infection by administering a single dose of vaccine,” said Dr Abhiyan Gautam, chief of the Immunisation Section at the Family Welfare Division under the Department of Health Services. “But the problem is we don’t have a vaccination programme for adults.”

Experts say the government should launch vaccination for all age groups, especially in high-risk areas.

“The government’s prime responsibility is saving lives,” said Dr Yasho Vardan Pradhan, former director general at the Department of Health Services. “JE infection is so deadly that even if patients survive, the virus leaves some lifelong effects.”

Along with vaccination, health officials say awareness drives, improved sanitation and hygiene, and behavioural changes are crucial in reducing transmission. Pigs and ducks are natural reservoirs of the virus. Pig farmers and those residing near the paddy fields are at particularly high risk of infection.

An estimated 12.5 million people in Nepal are thought to be at high risk of JE infection.

Officials at the Ministry of Health and Food Safety say they are exploring the possibility of administering a single dose of the JE vaccine to the entire adult population, but add that funding the programme would be difficult.

“We will hold discussions with relevant officials and explore possibilities,” said Dr Manohar Pradhan, Health Minister Nisha Mehta’s expert advisor. “We have discussed starting the vaccination from Koshi province, where the death rate is extremely high.”

articles.title: 500 documents vanished from the foreign ministry. Nepal never followed the trail
articles.summary:
Fifteen years after 500 blank travel documents disappeared from the Foreign Ministry’s store section, a chargesheet filed at the Kathmandu District Court has forced investigators to reopen a case they had left unresolved.

Last month, the District Attorney’s Office in Kathmandu filed a case against Pushpa Raj Bhattarai, a joint secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, over the illegal issuance of travel documents to five Tibetan refugees back in 2009. The case followed a years-long investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CIB), which the foreign ministry had asked to look into the matter in October 2011 — after a German Embassy official flagged, in 2010, that recently arrived Tibetan refugees appeared to be travelling on Nepali travel documents they should not have been able to obtain.

But buried inside Bhattarai’s chargesheet is a second, larger story: three of the five travel documents in question — bearing serial numbers A-026225, A-026226 and A-026227 — belong to a batch of 500 travel documents, numbered A-026001 to A-026500, that went missing from the Store Section in 2009 and were never accounted for. The other 497 have never been traced.

AIG Uma Prasad Chaturvedi, chief of the CIB, confirmed that a supplementary investigation into the remaining documents has now begun.

“The CIB has begun a supplementary investigation into who was involved in the other travel documents that went missing from the ministry at the time and where the misuse took place,” Chaturvedi told Kantipur. “The remaining matters will become clear only after the investigation.”

The missing documents first surfaced during an unrelated investigation in January 2010, when the CIB arrested Bachchuram KC, a non-gazetted officer in the Passport Section, for helping 30 foreign nationals — including five Afghans — obtain Nepali passports using forged documents. KC disclosed information about a wider network, and it was in the course of that inquiry that investigators discovered 500 travel documents had left the Store Section without ever reaching their stated destination.

According to a former joint secretary at the ministry who recalled the case, storekeeper Anil Lamsal released 250 documents intended for Nepal’s mission in Cairo and another 250 for its mission in Bangkok; KC received them for dispatch. But an internal check found that neither mission had actually requested the documents.

“How did the Cairo mission, the Passport Section and the Store Section fail to match up? A recommendation from the Ministry of Home Affairs is mandatory for issuing travel documents to refugees,” the former joint secretary told Kantipur. “Why was that requirement not considered necessary in this case? Why were documents that had not been requested released? These questions never became part of the investigation.”

KC told investigators that people in Nepal and India were involved in obtaining Nepali citizenship certificates for foreign nationals — for as much as $5,000 each — which were then used to secure Nepali passports. Despite being at the centre of the case, KC was never chargesheeted. He was transferred to the National Planning Commission and died on August 21, 2019.

A police officer involved in the original investigation, now an SSP, said the missing documents never got the scrutiny they warranted. “The investigation that should have taken place did not happen for reasons I am not aware of,” the officer told Kantipur, speaking on condition of anonymity.

An investigating officer from that period was more blunt about the outcome. “The documents never reached, or were never taken to, the two missions,” he said. “It has become mysterious as to why no investigation was carried out.” He believes the people responsible could still be identified if an impartial investigation were conducted now.

The CIB’s questioning of Bhattarai, along with two other former Passport Section officials — Ram Prasad Subedi and Anil Lamsal — is what eventually reconnected the two episodes. All three now hold senior diplomatic postings: Subedi is Nepal’s permanent representative to the United Nations in Geneva; Lamsal is first secretary at the Embassy of Nepal in Vienna.

In his statement to the CIB, recorded in the chargesheet, Subedi said he verified applicants and signed off on travel documents and passports that had come through proper channels, and denied any knowledge that KC had received 500 documents from the Store Section. “I had no knowledge that KC had received 500 travel documents from the Store Section and misused them,” he said.

Lamsal similarly denied involvement. “Travel documents released from the store section were entered in the register there and then sent to the dispatch section... to be forwarded to the concerned missions and embassies,” he told investigators. “I do not know where those travel documents went or where they were delivered afterwards.”

Surendra Thapa, now acting ambassador to India, told investigators he had occasionally signed and issued passports and travel documents in the Passport Section when Subedi was on leave or workload was high, but said he had no knowledge of the missing batch. Thapa was transferred to the ministry’s contact office in Birgunj on February 1, 2010.

Lok Bahadur Paudel Chhetri, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said the ministry’s hands are tied while the case is before the court. “The issue is very old, and since a related issue is sub judice, there is no particular information I can provide at this time,” he told Kantipur. “The concerned section must have looked into it as well; beyond that, I cannot say anything.”

The vulnerability the missing documents exposed was not new. A year earlier, in August 2008, two passengers were stopped at Tribhuvan International Airport before boarding a Gulf Air flight to Bahrain, en route to the United States on valid-looking US visas.

Their Nepali passports had been issued based on citizenship certificates that, on closer inspection, did not hold up. The two told immigration officials they were siblings travelling to meet their parents in Boston, and both named Dal Bahadur Lama as their father. But investigators found that Shekhar Kumar Adhikari, whose signature appeared on the citizenship certificates as the issuing officer, had never worked at the Kathmandu District Administration Office where the certificates were purportedly issued. The certificates were also dated November 9, 2007 — a public holiday for Tihar.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed the passports themselves were genuine, issued on January 22, 2008. The two individuals were prosecuted for forging government seals and signatures, and subsequently released on a Rs 9,000 bail. The trail stopped there. No one established where they went afterwards, who Dal Bahadur Lama was, or who had produced certificates that did not exist in government records but were nonetheless accepted as the basis for real passports.

Taken together with the 500 missing documents a year later, the case illustrates a recurring gap: Nepal’s passport-issuing system has repeatedly been shown capable of accepting fraudulent underlying documents without an agency ever establishing where those documents came from — and, in at least one case, without ever fully investigating where the resulting passports and travel documents went.

It is unclear how long the CIB’s supplementary investigation to look into the missing travel documents will take. “The remaining matters will become clear only after the investigation,” CIB chief Chaturvedi said.

articles.title: KU info lab leads efforts to digitise and preserve Nepal’s indigenous languages
articles.summary:
Communities and academics in Nepal are stepping up their efforts to put the country’s indigenous languages on the digital scene, aided by artificial intelligence that has emerged as an important tool for preserving languages and passing them on to the younger generation.

A major step comes from the Kathmandu University’s Information and Language Processing Research Lab, which recently unveiled a trilingual translation system covering Nepali, Tamang and English.

The system, supported by a Google Academic Research Award, was trained on more than 100,000 parallel sentences in Nepali, Tamang and English. Researchers used artificial intelligence and trained Meta AI’s NLLB-200 model on datasets in Nepali and Tamang.

Professor Bal Krishna Bal, lead researcher at the lab, said most of the information Nepali speakers find online is available either in English or Nepali. He believes the trilingual machine translation system can help Tamang speakers access the vast body of knowledge available online while allowing their culture and traditions to reach wider audiences.

“English has become so dominant that we find it increasingly difficult to write and speak even in Nepali. The language faces ever more encroachment,” Bal said.

“But among Nepalis living abroad, there seems to be a stronger emphasis on preserving their mother tongue. They want their children to learn cultural and family traditions, including customs and rules surrounding marriage.”

The usefulness of translation technology is broad, both inside Nepal and among Nepali communities abroad, Bal added.

Amrit Yonjan, coordinator of the Tamang translation team, said that the technology had given fresh hope to efforts to preserve Nepal’s indigenous languages. He added that the team was also working to have Tamang added to Google Translate by mid-March 2027.

“Google sent us some sentences in English. We translated them into Tamang and submitted them. They said they would integrate them into Google Translate,” Bal said.

“Before adding a new language, Google requires its own designated English-language corpus to be translated into the target language. We will soon complete that work and submit it.”

Nepali, Maithili and Nepal Bhasha, also known as Newari, are currently the only three languages from Nepal available on Google Translate.

The progress with Tamang has encouraged other linguistic communities to pursue similar projects. Magar, Sherpa and Tharu communities are among those showing interest in bringing their languages into AI systems.

The Magar and Tharu communities have already expressed their interest in formally working with Kathmandu University’s language research lab. The Magar community has pledged to provide more than 25,000 sentences and words to help researchers train an AI model.

Bishnu Kumar Sinjali, an activist involved in indigenous language and cultural studies, said the decline of his mother tongue was a serious concern.

Of Nepal’s estimated two million Magars, around 1.1 million have stopped speaking their mother tongue, he said.

“Technology has become essential to teaching the mother tongue to younger generations and ensuring its continuity,” Sinjali said.

“When languages are built into technology, it makes it easier for the government to provide services and conduct official business [in them]. Machines can make these processes more efficient without requiring too many personnel.”

For the transmission of linguistic knowledge from one generation to the next, embracing digital technology has become a necessity, he stressed.

Nepal’s constitution recognises Nepali, written in the Devanagari script, as the official language for federal government business under Article 7. Provinces can designate other mother tongues as official languages based on recommendations from the Language Commission.

The Koshi provincial government recently decided to move ahead with legislation to recognise Limbu and Maithili as languages for official business.

Among Nepal’s indigenous languages, Nepal Bhasha has made the most systematic progress in the digital sphere.

The language’s historic Ranjana and Prachalit scripts have been standardised in Unicode. Users can now access mobile keyboards, digital dictionaries, Google Translate and optical character recognition tools that can identify characters in historical inscriptions.

The Kathmandu Metropolitan City has also been active in supporting such efforts, including providing financial assistance to young people working on language digitisation. Acting mayor Sunita Dangol has herself been involved in promoting the digital use of the Ranjana script.

Another project, Newa ASR, led by young engineer Swarnim Nakarmi, is working to keep Nepal Bhasha alive through AI.

The automatic speech recognition project aims to develop systems capable of understanding and speaking Nepal Bhasha, including speech recognition and text-to-speech functions.

More than 35,000 voice samples have so far been collected through community participation, Nakarmi said.

“We have collected a wide range of voice samples from native Nepal Bhasha speakers from different regions and linguistic backgrounds,” he said. “The samples are processed and used to train a deep-learning model based on the phonetics and grammar of Nepal Bhasha. Our goal is to collect 100,000 voice samples to make the model more accurate and mature.”

Once completed, the technology will allow computers and other digital devices to understand Nepal Bhasha and accurately convert spoken language into written text. It will also be able to convert the Nepal Bhasha script into speech.

Kathmandu metropolis has also been recognised for its efforts to preserve local languages.

Aided by the municipal government, a Nepal Bhasha Dictionary app has been launched in coordination with cultural scholar Mall K Sundar. According to city spokesperson Nabin Manandhar, the app contains more than 41,000 words and their meanings. It also allows Romanised Nepali to be converted into Newa script.

“Language preservation cannot have a strong foundation if technology is ignored. People no longer have much time to sit down and read books,” Manandhar said

“The metropolis invested in creating an environment where people can find a word with a single click on their mobile phone. If needed, the City will also support Tamang and other indigenous languages spoken in Kathmandu.”

Kathmandu University and Kathmandu Metropolitan City have also worked together on an AI-based project to digitally archive ancient historical heritage sites in the Valley.

According to Professor Bal, researchers are developing technology that can photograph inscriptions whose characters are gradually being eroded by exposure to sunlight, rain and wind and convert them into digital text.

“We have developed a model that can photograph the inscriptions and convert their characters into digital text,” Bal said. “This is an important area of research from a historical and cultural perspective. But for now, it remains at the research stage. We have prepared the datasets and model, but it has yet to be released as an application or website.”

The push to bring Nepal’s languages into the digital world comes amid growing international concern over the lack of technological support for many of the world’s languages.

Last year, UNESCO released its report, “Global Roadmap for Multilingualism in the Digital Era: Advancing the Role of Language Technologies”, which called for inclusive language technologies, data sovereignty and community-led decision-making to help preserve mother tongues.

The UN agency has also set out strategies to ensure universal access to machine translation and language technologies across language communities and to support the digital transformation and promotion of endangered, indigenous, sign and haptic languages.

UNESCO has also been supporting young developers, startups and language advocates in Nepal through grants and other assistance as part of its strategy to promote multilingualism in the digital age.

One such initiative is Archive Nepal, which is working to preserve handwritten Nepal Bhasha manuscripts. With UNESCO’s support, the organisation has digitised more than 3,300 pages of old Nepal Bhasha manuscripts, said Saroja Hakuduwal, its operations manager. Young volunteers have transcribed and translated the manuscripts and uploaded them to Wikisource.

“Between November 2025 and August 2026, we digitised more than 30 rare Nepal Bhasha manuscripts that are between 200 and 800 years old,” Hakuduwal said. “With the help of volunteers, we are transcribing the manuscripts into digital text and translating them into Nepali and English so they are accessible to the public. The materials are freely available on Wikisource and Archive Nepal’s digital platform.”

Archive Nepal has also organised four “Transcribathon” events to teach people how to read the Ranjana, Prachalit and Bhujimol scripts and type them using Unicode. More than 50 volunteers from different generations have taken part.

For some young participants, it was their first opportunity to learn to read and type their own traditional script, Hakuduwal said.

“At our fourth Transcribathon event, we brought together AI developers working on Nepal Bhasha speech recognition technology and visual artists to demonstrate how modern technology and art can be combined to preserve traditional cultural heritage,” she said. “We now plan to digitise old materials in other languages as well. We are studying whether ancient and historical manuscripts kept in Tibetan monasteries can also be digitised.”

To understand how these efforts to preserve mother tongues through technology have evolved, it is worth looking back at Nepal’s history of language digitisation.

Writer Kedar Sharma, who played a leading role in promoting Unicode to make Nepali easier to use on computers and the internet, says technology has opened new possibilities for indigenous languages that once struggled even to gain a foothold in the digital world.

In the early days, he said, bringing languages into digital technology was expensive and difficult.

“When the Madan Puraskar Pustakalaya was developing a Unicode keyboard, computers and other tools were extremely expensive, consumed a lot of electricity, and mobile phones had not yet arrived,” Sharma recalled. “The biggest obstacle, however, was the language itself. People who did not know English could barely use a computer. When Android technology came to Nepal, it gave indigenous languages a new lease of life.”

The spread of Android and social media created new opportunities for people to write and express themselves in their own languages, Sharma said. He finds that important not only for language preservation but also for social progress and dignity.

The disappearance of a language, he said, means far more than the loss of words. It can also erase generations of knowledge and local traditions embedded in that language.

“Traditional knowledge held by older people, such as identifying and eating different plants and preparing food using resources from villages and forests, can disappear along with a language,” Sharma said. “Digital preservation of languages is therefore crucial for passing on the knowledge our society has accumulated over thousands of years.”

He said some families are increasingly choosing to teach their children only Nepali and English, rather than their mother tongue, as they become more integrated into the linguistic mainstream.

AI for Nepal’s languages

Himalaya AI Labs is also working to build a local AI ecosystem, with a focus on Nepali and other low-resource languages that have relatively little content available online.

The organisation is developing Devanagari-focused datasets and foundation models for Nepali and other languages. It is also building benchmark tests to measure the accuracy and performance of AI models and developing datasets to improve Nepali-language processing, translation and output quality using open-source models.

Himalaya AI is working with international and Nepali researchers based abroad to secure computing and GPU infrastructure. It aims to develop a large language model focused on Nepali, with plans eventually to bring regional languages such as Rai, Limbu and Newari into AI systems.

Sharma believes technology could even help revive languages that are declining.

“I see strong potential for language revival,” he said. “Having the tools available and growing ethnic and cultural awareness within communities can make a huge difference.”

During the Panchayat era, he recalled, recording a song required access to Radio Nepal or Ratna Recording Studio because recording technology was limited and tightly controlled by the state.

“But once FM radio stations began operating and recording technology became more accessible, songs and creative works in Newari, Tamang, Kirat and other local tongues grew rapidly,” he said. “Once technology gives us the tools, the responsibility to use them and take them forward rests with the people who speak that language.”

Government efforts lag

While communities, researchers and technology groups are moving ahead, the government’s response remains slower.

The Language Commission began work on a multilingual electronic dictionary in the fiscal year 2018-19, but the project has yet to be completed.

The commission has so far entered words from 30 languages into its digital dictionary, said spokesperson Kamala Bhandari Pandey.

“The commission has developed multilingual electronic dictionary software that allows words to be easily interpreted from one language to another,” the commission said in its seventh annual report. “In addition, around 6,200 Nepali words have been entered and linked, wherever possible, to entries in each language.”

The software already contains vocabulary from languages including Athpahariya, Uranw, Chamling, Chhantyal, Darai, Bote, Bajjika, Yakkha, Lungkhim, Santhali, Sampang, Belhare, Kathariya Tharu, Done, Jumli, Thulung, Limbu, Tajpuriya, Kshetteli, Tilung, Dangaura Tharu, and Raute.

But a lack of funding has stalled further development, Pandey said.

“Because of budget constraints, we have not been able to further improve the software, and it is still not open to the general public,” she said. “The government’s practice of slashing the budget each year and failing to prioritise language preservation has slowed these efforts.”

Linguists and language activists are critical of the government’s slow pace.

With AI developing at such speed, they say there is little time to waste if indigenous languages are to remain relevant in the digital world. Languages unable to keep pace with new technologies face the threat of gradual extinction.

“Ultimately, the government needs to take ownership of this work and support it to make it sustainable,” Bal said. “Local and provincial governments, in particular, have an important role to play.”

articles.title: Why we should protect Nepal’s pluralism from opportunists
articles.summary:
In Nepali politics, principles have often been traded as cheap currency. Still, the recent spectacle of Sher Bahadur Deuba, former prime minister and immediate past president of the Nepali Congress, executing a theological about-face is particularly disquieting. Having spent his years at the helm of the grand old party actively suppressing the Mahasamiti’s fervour for a return to a Hindu state, Deuba has abruptly emerged as its champion. Upon his return from East Asia amidst money-laundering investigations and Congress’s leadership change, he unceremoniously ordered his faction’s national gathering to endorse the very agenda he previously blocked repeatedly.

This is a political manoeuvre of a displaced leader attempting to establish relevance.

To understand the utter hypocrisy of this pivot, examine Deuba’s own record. During the constitutional debates of 2015, and as recently as the Mahasamiti meetings of 2018 and 2024, Deuba rejected petitions to depart from constitutional secularism signed by hundreds of party members. In his years of power, Deuba repeatedly warned that such reversal of secularism would invite division in society. Now, unseated by a special general convention and pursued by legal scrutiny, he weaponises religion as a shield. He is neither alone nor the first to indulge in this brand of opportunism. Senior politicians have historically used religious cards to keep their business afloat at the expense of festering divisions in society.

The Congress’s deposed leader is better off accepting that the separation of religion from governance is the very bedrock of civic peace. If he is looking for reasoning to change his current stance, he could turn to Jean-Jacques Rousseau, who argued that religions inevitably divide a citizen’s loyalty, as one cannot fully commit to the laws of the state whilst caught between secular duties and the decrees of a religion. If Deuba needs further logic, he could dig up Immanuel Kant’s argument that when a government uses religious doctrines to enforce laws, it treats its citizens like children, demanding obedience through divine fear rather than respecting them as rational, autonomous adults capable of moral choices. By mixing the spiritual with the political, Deuba has infantilised the Nepali populace, reducing a complex, pluralistic republic to a congregation.

The real-world consequences of this ideological regression are already visible in regional friction. Pushing a pro-Hindu political agenda systematically alienates Nepal’s significant religious and ethnic minorities—Buddhists, Muslims, Christians, and Kirat communities—relegating them to second-class status. We need only recall the recent communal clashes in the southern plains, where a trivial dispute over loudspeakers rapidly amplified, transforming neighbours into adversaries and prompting curfews.

Moreover, the religious shift cannot be separated from geopolitical shadows. Analysts point to the majoritarian influence of religion-based politics in neighbouring states, where the mainstreaming of religious nationalism has led to systemic polarisation. This model has bled across borders, emboldening Nepal’s own regressive groups. By copying this majoritarian pattern, Nepal risks inviting the structural decay seen elsewhere in the region—from the Buddhist nationalism in Sri Lanka’s civil war to the Rohingya crisis in Myanmar.

Politics is the art of compromise and pragmatism. Religion deals in the absolute. When the absolute is dragged into the mud of political factionalism, both are corrupted. In Nepal’s context, secularism was one of the hardest-won compromises of a decade-long civil war that dismantled a feudal Hindu monarchy to build an inclusive republic. It cannot be sacrificed on the altar of one man’s desperate quest for political survival. If Deuba’s faction succeeds in dragging the Congress down this sectarian path, they will set fire to Nepal’s constitutional foundations.

Nepal’s future lies in looking forward, not backwards. The gods do not belong in the realm of politics. Deuba might succeed in commanding the support of regressive religious groups with his ideological pivot, but his deliberate divine deception must be rejected by both the public and his faction’s cadres.

articles.title: What Happens When Real Technocrats Take the Wheel?
articles.summary:
Nepal’s economic institutions have always been physically close to one another. Around Thapathali, Maitighar and Singha Durbar, the country’s central-banking, planning and finance offices sit within a short distance of one another. Yet for much of our modern history, fiscal policy and monetary policy have often moved as if they belonged to different worlds.

A finance ministry under political pressure naturally looks toward spending, public promises, and visible relief. A central bank, responsible for prices, reserves, credit and financial stability, is often forced to act as the institutional brake. One side is accused of being reckless; the other is accused of being too cautious. The result is a familiar cycle: Budgetary ambition is undercut by monetary tightening, while monetary discipline is weakened by fiscal pressure. The state remains busy, but not always coherent.

This is why the present alignment between the Ministry of Finance and Nepal Rastra Bank deserves attention. With Swarnim Wagle at the finance ministry and Biswo Nath Poudel at the central bank, Nepal has two economists with serious academic training occupying two of the most important positions in the country’s economic governance. What matters most is the academic rigour behind their public reputations, a quality still too rare in Nepal’s political life.

Public life often rewards visibility, factional strength and tactical agility, but it less often rewards deep study, long preparation and technical command.
